cards.explanation: The answer is firstfruits. Moses says, “…take some of the firstfruits of all your produce from the soil of the land…” That's the first of the harvest going in the basket. When a tray comes out of my oven, that first cookie gets ALL the attention, so I can picture how special first-of-the-batch is.

The worshiper declares that he has entered the land the LORD swore to give. The words are, “I declare today to the LORD your God that I have entered the land that the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.” Notice who did the swearing: the LORD did. The worshiper is standing there with a basket as proof that the promise came through.

The answer is False. The worshiper says the wandering Aramean went down to Egypt “…few in number…” It was after he lived there that he “…became a great nation, mighty and numerous.” Small family on the way in, great nation by the time the story gets going, friends.

The answer is that He hears their voice and sees their affliction. The worshiper says, “…the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, toil, and oppression.” They called out, and He heard and saw. Two actions, friends, and both belong to the LORD. I think that's a comfort.

The answer is that He brought them to this land flowing with milk and honey. The worshiper says, “And He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.” Notice the word “gave.” The land is a gift, and the basket in his hands is what the gift grew.

The answer is True, friends. Moses says, “Then you are to place the basket before the LORD your God and bow down before Him.” So the basket is set before the LORD, and then the worshiper bows down. Basket down, then bow down. I like that order.

The answers are rejoices and foreigner. Moses says, “So you shall rejoice…in all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household.” He says to rejoice with “…the Levite, and the foreigner dwelling among you…” That's a person just living among them, and the text hands them a seat at the celebration. I know a little about being the new one in the room, and a seat at the table is a beautiful thing.

The answer is True. In the third year, the year of the tithe, Moses says to give it to four groups: the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow. The reason he gives is that they may eat and be filled within the gates. I count four names on that list, and the tithe is for every one of them.

The answer is False. The giver declares, “I have not eaten any of the sacred portion while in mourning, or removed any of it while unclean, or offered any of it for the dead.” It's a list of things he says he did not do. He's not admitting to anything, and I'd say that's a pretty confident thing to say out loud.

The giver sums it up by saying he has done everything the LORD commanded. The words are, “I have obeyed the LORD my God; I have done everything You commanded me.” Everything. That's a big word to say out loud in front of the LORD, and the giver says it.

The answers are bless and land. The giver says, “Look down from Your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the land You have given us as You swore to our fathers…” That's the request that follows all the giving, as he turns from what he did to what he's asking the LORD to do. He's asking for blessing on the people and on the place they live, and once again the land is called a gift.

The answer is with all their heart and all their soul. Moses says, “You must be careful to follow them with all your heart and with all your soul.” That's all of it, not just a piece. I think that's a fair way to say it, friends: halfway doesn't make a good batch of anything.

The answer is that they are His people and treasured possession. Moses says, “And today the LORD has proclaimed that you are His people and treasured possession as He promised…” Treasured is a warm word, friends. It's the kind of thing you say about something you keep close.

The answer is True, friends. Moses says the LORD will set Israel high above all the nations He has made, in praise, name and honor. That's three things. The verse adds that Israel will be a holy people to the LORD, as He has promised.
